(Kitco News) – China’s 2026 gold imports could be double those of last year, and will set the high-water mark for the 2020s to date, while silver prices are approaching a key test that could determine the gray metal’s near-term direction, according to precious metals analysts at Heraeus.
In their latest update, the analysts noted that China’s gold imports have already exceeded 2025 totals in 2026. “China imported 142 tonnes of gold in August, taking imports during the first eight months of the year to 1,141 tonnes, 72% higher than the 663 tonnes imported over the same period last year, and higher than the 940 tonnes imported during the whole of 2025,” they wrote. “The strong inflows come despite historically high gold prices and reflect continued investment demand, while Chinese jewellery demand remains comparatively weak. These non-monetary imports are separate from purchases by the People’s Bank of China, which added a further 20 tonnes to its official reserves in August.”
“If Chinese gold imports maintain this pace through the rest of 2026, they will total ~1,700 tonnes, which would represent the highest amount this decade.”
Australia’s gold mine production continued to rise in fiscal year 2025-26 as historically high prices continue to support the mining sector. “Australia produced 303 tonnes of gold up to the end of its financial year in June, broadly in line with its long-run production rate of around 300 tonnes p.a.,” the analysts said. “Output improved at most operations during the June quarter, while several smaller producers also began production. The 303 tonnes produced in Australia account for around 8% of total mined gold supply, which was 3,822 tonnes in 2025.”
Heraeus said Indonesia is proposing a scheme to incentivize privately held gold stocks to be invested into the formal financial system. “The government estimates that households hold around 1,800 tonnes of gold outside formal investment channels and has asked state-owned institutions to encourage around 20% of this metal, equivalent to roughly 360 tonnes, into bullion-banking and financial products,” they wrote. “The initiative is aimed at turning privately held metal into deposits, collateral and other financial assets, deepening the domestic bullion market and potentially increasing the amount of household wealth circulating through the financial system.”
The analysts also warned that India’s weak monsoon will likely depress rural gold demand during this year’s festival and wedding season – and rural demand represents over 50% of the country’s total bullion consumption. “Monsoon rainfall was around 15% below its long-run average by late September, presenting a downside risk to gold demand due to the potential of lower crop yields to impact rural incomes,” they said. “Historical analysis by the World Gold Council suggests that a 1% increase in rainfall relative to the average is associated with a 0.2% increase in gold demand, implying that this year’s rainfall deficit could represent a modest headwind. Indian gold demand totalled 768 tonnes in 2025, roughly 15% of global demand.”
Spot gold was continuing to test session lows early in the North American session, and last traded at $4,142.30 for a loss of 3.33% on the daily chart.
Turning to silver, Heraeus analysts noted that the renewed strength of the U.S. dollar has driven silver prices to a key inflection point.
“Silver prices dropped below $65/oz last week as the dollar index rose back above 101.0, towards its yearly highs,” they noted. “This leaves silver at an important level. A renewed rally back towards $70/oz despite a rising dollar, a hawkish Federal Reserve and rising bond yields could signal a confirmation of a potential bottoming process. However, if silver falls back below $60/oz, this could be the sign of a continuation of the bearish downtrend, marked by lower highs and lower lows, in which silver has been stuck since its late January peak.”
The analysts wrote that the 10-year Treasury yield’s rise to 5.22% and the 10-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Security (TIPS) real yield hitting 2.8% indicates that the Federal Reserve’s 25 basis point rate hike in September was not enough to reassure markets.
“The rise in real yields alongside nominal yields is particularly significant for precious metals, indicating that the sell-off in Treasuries has not been driven solely by higher inflation expectations, but also by investors demanding a higher inflation-adjusted return, consistent with the anticipation that monetary policy could remain tighter for longer,” they said. “This comes as Brent crude remains around $100/bbl, and despite renewed talks between the US and Iran, a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz does not appear imminent.”
And Indian silver imports spiked higher in August after several months of weak inflows. “India imported 15.5 moz of silver in August, the first time since February that monthly imports have topped 10 moz and 36% higher than the 11.4 moz imported in August 2025,” the analysts wrote. “Despite the strong monthly recovery, imports remain weak for the year as a whole, with an estimated 75.6 moz imported during January-August, 24% less than the 99.1 moz imported over the same period last year.”
“The rebound follows several months of unusually low imports after the licensing requirements introduced in May complicated the import process and high silver prices reduced demand, they said. “The upswing in August suggests that physical inflows are beginning to normalise, although year-to-date imports remain well below last year’s levels.”
Silver prices were also trading just above their earlier session lows on Monday morning after dipping below $61 per ounce around 5 am ET.

If you’re an avid Gemini user and have created a bunch of Gemini Gems tailored to your needs and preferences, we have good and bad news for you today. After months of hearing about Google’s plans to sunset Gems in favor of Skills, and finding code in the Google app hinting at the same, Google has finally made an official announcement.
Opening the Gems manager in Gemini now shows a banner announcing Google’s plan to end Gems support starting November 17. That’s the bad news, but there’s a bit of good news as well, though with some confusion that Google has yet to clear up.
According to the banner, Google will start “migrating your Gems to Skills” starting November 17, and you will be able to use your Gems until they are migrated. Theoretically, this could take longer than a few days, which makes it seem as though your Gems might last for a few extra days past that mid-November deadline. You will also be able to continue using your Gems in the form of Skills once they are migrated, so you won’t lose all the work you put into them.
The confusing part lies in Google’s plans for giving users access to Skills. While Gems are available to all users, including those with free accounts, Skills are (as of right now) only available to those with a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription and access to Gemini Spark .
If Google migrates Gems to Skills, is it also planning to let users with free accounts create and access Skills in Gemini? That would be the logical conclusion. However, the “Learn More” button in the banner currently leads to a Google Support page that doesn’t exist. That page will likely include a more detailed explanation of Google’s plans regarding Skills access for free accounts.
For now, you should prepare for Gems to go away in a little over a month’s time. Here’s hoping Google won’t just hang free users out to dry, migrating their Gems to Skills and forcing them to upgrade to a Google AI Pro or Ultra account to access those Skills.
We have reached out to Google for comment and will update this story when we hear back.

articles.title_orig: Trump Brought Venezuelan Gold to the U.S., but Refiners Won’t Touch It
articles.title_zh: Trump Brought Venezuelan Gold to the U.S., but Refiners Won’t Touch It
articles.content_orig:
Gold imported from Venezuela under a US-backed deal remains in warehouses as refiners seek assurances over its origin and possible links to criminal groups, according to a report published Monday.
The Trump administration opened the US market to Venezuelan gold in March as Washington expanded economic ties with Venezuela’s interim government led by Delcy Rodriguez.
The New York Times reported that Minerven, Venezuela’s state-owned gold mining company, reached an agreement with Trafigura, a global commodities trading company, to supply gold for the US market.
Trafigura agreed to purchase between 650 and 1,000 kilograms (1,433 and 2,205 pounds) of gold dore bars from Minerven. The gold was shipped to the US for refining and resale.
US refiners have declined to purchase some of the gold because they cannot certify that it was obtained without involvement from criminal groups, illegal mining or other illicit activities, according to the report.
Informal mining operations in southern Venezuela provide part of their gold production to the Tren de Guayana criminal group in exchange for protection, The New York Times reported.
A leader of one mining operation told the newspaper that about 20% of its gold production is given to the group.
The newspaper also reported that Trafigura purchased millions of dollars worth of gold before independent auditors inspected the mines involved in the agreement.
Trafigura said its due diligence process was ongoing. The company said audits of sites it had inspected found no evidence of human rights violations, conflict financing, illegal taxation, extortion or involvement by illegal actors.
The company plans to source gold from two industrial mines under military protection to reduce the risk of criminal groups entering the supply chain.
Minerven remains under US sanctions, while the Trump administration has authorized transactions involving Venezuelan gold as part of its broader policy toward Caracas.
The agreement comes as Washington seeks to expand economic ties with Venezuela and gain greater access to the country’s mineral resources.

articles.title_orig: Turtle Beach Afterglow Review: A Switch 2 Controller With The Full RGB Treatment
articles.title_zh: Turtle Beach Afterglow Review: A Switch 2 Controller With The Full RGB Treatment
articles.content_orig:
This is for the gamer who wants RGB everything.
Maybe I'm feeding into a stereotype, perhaps it makes me a basic gamer, but dang it — I love RGB lighting. I want it in my keyboard, mouse, PC case, headphones, game consoles and behind every screen in the house, layering a subtle sci-fi glow over my entire space. At night, I want to fall asleep beneath shifting rainbow galaxies. I want to cradle an LED prism in my hands. Even better if it can control my video games, too.
You see where this is heading. The Turtle Beach Afterglow Wireless Controller for Nintendo Switch 2 is a transparent gamepad with variable RGB light settings, and it looks like a handheld cosmic gemstone. On top of its aesthetic allure, the Switch 2 Afterglow is a responsive, low-latency controller with a wireless range of up to 30 feet and ultra-precise TMR thumbsticks, which provide a long-term drift-free guarantee. In action, the gamepad is nicely reactive and comfortable to hold for hours on end, with hard, clicky face buttons, cushioned trigger pulls and mappable rear paddles that can be super satisfying fidget toys when not actually in use. The back buttons function independently, but they're connected by a matte black bridge, adding a secondary sensory pop beneath the opposite fingertip with each press.
Aside from an additional strip of shiny black between the triggers and shoulder buttons, housing the USB-C charging point and bluetooth connection, the controller chassis is clear plastic. Even the grips aren't textured, lending the whole thing a crisp, crystalline look whether the lights are off or on. Switch 2 controllers tend to be rather small and light, a fact that I personally love, and the Afterglow fits this description. It's similar in size and weight to the official Switch 2 Pro Controller, the console's reigning standard. Of course, the Pro costs $90 while the Afterglow costs $65 and is often on sale for far less.
The lack of texture on the grips hasn't been an issue for me, even after playing Resident Evil Requiem for a few hours to really test out the sweat factor. The Switch 2 Afterglow is comfortable to hold for long periods of time; it's never unexpectedly slipped out of my hands or threatened to throw off my zombie-hunting game in first- or third-person. It also handles Hello Kitty Island Adventure like a champ.
The Afterglow's buttons are black with symbols and letters etched into the faces, which brings me to a gripe I have with nearly all Switch 2 controllers, including Nintendo's own: The minus, plus, home and other small face buttons are nearly impossible to read. This fact is particularly frustrating when you're using a gamepad for the first time and getting used to its layout. The Switch 2 Afterglow, for instance, has a dedicated GameChat button in the center of the array, plus and minus buttons above that, and Home and Capture above those. I accidentally took a handful of random screenshots while reaching blindly for the minus button to open the map in Requiem , and I was never quite able to shake off the incorrect muscle memory. I'd love if the icons were highlighted to make the small buttons more readable at a quick glance.
The Switch 2 Afterglow has motion-control capabilities but it doesn't feature any haptics, so there's no rumble here. Its analog sticks use top-of-the-line TMR technology, which promises long-term accuracy without the risk of drift, and they make a nice clacky sound when they hit the sides of their enclosures. The tops of the Afterglow thumbsticks have fairly high, defined edges with a textured divot for your thumbpad, and they're easy to press in even at an angle.
In the box, the Afterglow comes with a 1-meter charging cable and it boasts a battery life of 40 hours — but that's with no RGBs ( why? ). Turtle Beach's Switch 2 controllers generally get 12 hours of playtime with RGB lighting effects on, and that's likely to be the case here, too. This particular model isn't able to wake up the Switch 2, but it connects seamlessly to the console once it's on.
Now, let's talk about those RGBs.
The Afterglow has four lighting modes, adjustable by holding the small circle beneath the right thumbstick, and then pressing the L or R bumpers. The LED settings are as follows: On and steady, pulsing in one color, cycling through all colors, and reactive to stick movement. You're able to set the colors and adjust brightness on the fly as well, and it's all super simple. The lights are vibrant and fill the entirety of the gamepad with a clean radiance. The RGB instructions live right here , for quick reference.
My favorite setting is the input-responsive one, where the controller lights up in a specific color depending on which direction the analog stick travels, generating a rainbow light show as you play. But truly, the Afterglow makes me smile no matter which mode it's set to. Even off, it's a slick-looking gamepad.
But again, I'm a sucker for this stuff. I love transparent gadgets with their motherboards and mechanical guts exposed, and I adore RGB lights. The Turtle Beach Afterglow for Switch 2 combines these styles in a delicious way, and it happens to be a precise and responsive gamepad, to boot. I'm happy to have one, here in my crystal kingdom.

articles.title_orig: Capitol agenda: Thune plots final votes before midterms
articles.title_zh: Capitol agenda: Thune plots final votes before midterms
articles.content_orig:
Ohio Senate race candidates clash over local energy costs and AI data centers as the 'Fox News Sunday' panel analyzes the upcoming midterm elections. The panel debates the political stakes of high utility bills and Chinese bot farm manipulation on social media. New polling shows a tight Senate race in Maine.
It’s a calculation by Republicans to keep the Senate in session this week.
Yes. The Senate was scheduled to meet anyway over the next few days. But the general consensus early last week was that the Senate would be done then, and those facing competitive races would be back home campaigning.
Republicans wanted to stay in Washington. For a very specific reason. And many of them told Senate Majority Leader John Thune , R-S.D., as much at their weekly luncheon.
"Odds are we plan on being here next week," said Thune.
REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS STRUGGLES TO FIND A MESSAGE THAT RESONATES WITH VOTERS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., speaks to reporters outside the chamber at the Capitol in Washington, Thursday, April 2, 2026. (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo)
One Senate aide compared the Senate’s schedule to a cat chasing a beam of light from a laser pointer.
But the Senate is in fact meeting. There are reasons. Most of them are political.
The Senate wasn’t quite done with the bill to regulate money in intercollegiate athletics last week. And with the affordability question vexing Republicans, they really didn’t want to pass the college sports bill and promptly vacate Washington. That would be an awkward punctuation point at the end of the legislative sentence before the midterms. GOPers wanted something more substantive. Democrats might have presented that opportunity to Republicans on a platter.
Before the House left for the midterms the week before last, it accentuated its session by passing the Ratepayer Protection Act , 417-3. Let me tell you, not much passes around here with 417 votes. Like their Senate colleagues, House Republicans also worry about voters doubting they’re addressing affordability. So this bill hit the mark for them.
The legislation defrays the costs ratepayers fork out for their utility bills if they’re driven up by data centers. This forces the tech companies which run the data centers to foot the bill.
Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, is one of the most vulnerable Republicans on the ballot this fall. Husted’s longtime support for data centers is also dragging him down in the eyes of some voters. Husted tried to fix that. He went to the floor and asked for the Senate to pass on the spot the House bill. However, Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., objected, blocking the effort.
FOX NEWS POLL: ECONOMIC ANXIETY AND CANDIDATE CONCERNS DEFINE OHIO SENATE RACE
Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., was one of the key members of the left to help get Sen. Jim Justice's Hershel Woody Williams bill passed unanimously in the Senate. (Elizabeth Frantz)
Republicans viewed that as an opening. Democrats stood in the way of passing a bill on affordability which 417 bipartisan House members supported without blinking. Senate GOPers immediately seized this opportunity as a wedge against their adversaries. And, they interpreted this as a chance to assist their Ohio colleague.
"Tell the data centers we're happy to have you. But you've got to pay your own electricity. People are not going to pay for it," said Sen. John Kennedy, R-La.
Republicans were already leery about the uneven political footing when it comes to AI. Even more so with data centers. Voters are not enamored with the results of the Big, Beautiful Bill, passed last summer. But dealing with data centers is more immediate and might resonate with those who soured on the Republican brand.
"In Missouri, people are absolutely scared to death that these data centers are going to take all the prime farm ground of the state. And then they're going to raise electricity bills so high, no one will be able to afford them," said Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo.
The official schedule intended for the Senate to meet this week. But once September hit and no government shutdown loomed, senators from both sides – especially those facing challenging elections – wanted to skip Washington and campaign back home. Yours truly asked Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., why his party stood in the way of the Senate aligning with the House on that data center/utilities measure.
"Was this blocked in the Senate last week by Democrats as an effort to prevent Sen. Husted from having a win in this competitive race?" I asked.
" Sen. Husted's bill is a fraud. It's voluntary. No company has to do it. The bill we have is mandatory. It is much stronger and is what is needed," replied Schumer.
There is something to Schumer’s argument about how muscular the bill is. The legislation says public utility regulators must only consider a standard for ratepayers. Nothing is required. Thus, there’s wiggle room for tech firms.
HAWLEY TAKES AIM AT 'CORPORATE WELFARE' AFTER GOP-BACKED TAX BREAK BOOSTED CONTROVERSIAL INDUSTRY
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, a Democrat from New York, speaks during a news conference following Senate Democratic policy luncheons at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday, June 23, 2026. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
"What we're saying is that we can do much better," said Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md. "Is it a little step forward? Yes. But it's not meeting the moment. So our view is we should expand it to make sure that ratepayers aren't having to subsidize the richest corporations on the planet."
But a lot of Republicans aren’t buying what Schumer and Van Hollen are saying. The Democratic objections are all about three things: Politics. An endangered GOP senator in the most expensive Senate contest in the country. And, Democrats are hoping to flip the seat in their favor.
"Sen. Schumer, what he cares about is the midterm election and politics. And I don't think he cares about the substance of this," said Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas. "Obviously there's a hot and heavy Senate race going on in Ohio, and he doesn't want to let Sen. Husted have something he can talk about when he goes home."
Republicans view the opportunity to turn the affordability issue against Democrats – capitalizing on Schumer’s remark and forcing Democrats to take a stand. Either you’re for affordability (especially as it pertains to the toxic issue of data centers) or you’re not. Moreover, this could boost Husted in his competitive contest with former Sen. Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio . In fact, it was the Senate GOP’s campaign arm which specifically flagged vulnerabilities for Republicans generally and Husted in particular over the summer.
Thune tees up a test vote on Wednesday to dare Democrats to either start debate on the bill or block it again. That vote requires 60 yeas. So Democratic cooperation is required. Although there’s skepticism anything happens, some Democrats may vote for it. That means the Senate is on the bill. And it’s open to debate and amendments. Thune would have to forge a bipartisan time agreement to finish the measure quickly.
Otherwise – by the book – this would drag into the weekend. And no one wants that. Especially Republicans with competitive races.
12 RACES SCRAMBLE SENATE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS EYE COMEBACK
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and the GOP are gearing up for a floor battle with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and Senate Democrats over Trump-backed voter ID legislation. (Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Thune and Schumer want senators back home campaigning. If Democrats impede the legislation Wednesday, the Senate might hang around Thursday or that’s it until after the midterms. Regardless, Republicans will have engineered a vote which they can boomerang against Democrats. Or, at least help Husted and send him back to the Buckeye State with a win.

articles.title_orig: Madonna’s ‘Danceteria’ Was One of the Great Moments in VMAs History
articles.title_zh: Madonna’s ‘Danceteria’ Was One of the Great Moments in VMAs History
articles.content_orig:
Madonna made her big return to the MTV Video Music Awards, her first time at the annual event in 23 years. She practically invented this show the first time it aired in 1984, making her infamous debut in her white wedding gown as the scandalous floor-humping bride in “Like a Virgin.” That performance did wonders for her, but even bigger wonders for the VMAs — it’s the moment this event has always aspired to match ever since. It established her as the once and future queen of this show. But strange as it seems, until Sunday night, she hadn’t rocked the VMAs since 2003, when she did an even better version of “Like a Virgin,” in her legendary make-out session with Britney Spears .
So the stakes were high for her hotly anticipated return Sunday night. But her amazing performance with Sabrina Carpenter and Charli XCX stole the show, with a medley of “One Step Away,” “Bring Your Love,” and “Danceteria,” from her recent Confessions II. It wasn’t just the highlight of the night; it was one of the most stunning performances in the entire history of the VMAs, hands down.
It’s fitting that she began with Sabrina, who was just four years old when Madonna smooched Britney, but a quintessential Daughter of the House of Ciccone. “It’s mother,” a voice moaned at the beginning, as Madonna recited her disco catechism. “The dance floor is not a place,” she said. “It’s a threshold. A ritualistic space where movement replaces language.”
#SabrinaCarpenter makes a surprise appearance during #Madonna ’s #VMAs performance. (via CBS/MTV/VMAs) pic.twitter.com/b7UtSqEilT
Wearing a black beret, Sabrina played the piano with Madonna writhing on top of it. They did their Coachella-slaying duet “Bring Your Love,” with Sabrina twisting and crawling in her glitter-spangled black liederhosen. Madonna wrestled with black-clad storm troopers, then got rolled on a gurney through the crowd, until a really confusing interlude where she met a bizarro alien gospel choir in white gowns. (A very Creed touch.)
But the performance really exploded when Charli XCX strutted in for “Danceteria,” as the stage transformed into the famous early-Eighties NYC disco, with the cool girls hanging out in the men’s room. Charli even stroked the bathroom hand dryer — a clever reference to everybody’s favorite scene in Desperately Seeking Susan .
CHARLI XCX PERFORMING ‘DANCETERIA AFTERHOURS’ WITH MADONNA pic.twitter.com/LbLrourkag
The “Danceteria” bathroom was jumping with party people. Over here, Madonna and Charli rocking out. Over there, Sombr posing as a scantily clad black-leather boy. Hey, look — it’s Debi Mazar, years before Goodfellas , just another party girl and Madonna’s coolest club-kid girlfriend, name-checked in the song. (Also, a callback to Debi’s cameo in the “Music” video from Y2K — maybe Madonna’s peak era ever?) Hey, that guy looks like … wait, it is Fab 5 Freddy, also namechecked. Julia Garner, dressed in the “Open Your Heart” black corset and haircut. Tony Ward, from the “Justify My Love” video. The “Boy Toy” belt buckle. Producer Andrew Watt, as Keith Haring. Seth Rogen … wait, really? What the hell is Seth doing here? Who dragged him to a disco? Ah, well — everybody’s welcome here. Anyone can be a star on Madonna’s dance floor. That’s the whole point of the song — as she keeps chanting, “Everybody here is a work of art.”
A clever detail: Lou Reed’s face on the “Danceteria” bathroom wall, the Mick Rock photo from the cover of his 1972 classic Transformer , as they all sang the “doo de doo de doo” hook from “Walk on the Wild Side.” (Watt walked the red carpet in a T-shirt displaying that Lou photo.) Given my unfortunately encyclopedic memory for trashy award shows, I can tell you this was Lou’s first cameo on the VMAs since 2006, when he and Jack White played “White Light/White Heat” with the Raconteurs.
Madonna made it all feel like a musical autobiography for her, doubling as a capsule history of club culture. It summed up where she came from, why she left, why she came to New York, and what she made of the dreams she worked to bring to life. That’s the theme of her excellent album Confessions II . But she packed the whole messy story into “Danceteria.” Related Content The VMAs: The One Night When MTV Pretends to be MTV Taylor Swift Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton While Accepting Video of the Year Award at 2026 VMAs GENER8ION and Yung Lean Premiere Electrifying Performance of ‘Storm II’ at 2026 VMAs Raye, Sombr, Teddy Swims, Adam Lambert Salute  George Michael at MTV VMAs
Madonna kept winning awards all night, giving magnificently chaotic, unprepared, and awkward speeches, yet still with more star power than anyone in the room. Her best moment: When she won the Best Dance category, she threw her arms around Charli and Troye Sivan and said, “I’m kind of unclear what this award is for?” You and us both, Madonna. Charli had to reread the envelope to confirm it was for her Confessions II short film. She complained about the mic stand being too high for her. She also did one of the most uncomfortable dad jokes ever heard on an award show, including the ones hosted by Billy Crystal: “First of all, I’d like to thank my fingers, because I can always count on them.” Why in God’s name did she say this? Madonna, you’re on live TV here. Hold it together. We’re rooting for you.
But even when she was making everyone squirm (poor Troye looked terrified), she was still the coolest, and she knew it, fully confident this was her show. She told the story of her 1984 “Like a Virgin” moment, and how her management team told her backstage that she’d just killed her career. “My dress went up, and my butt cheek was hanging out,” she recalled. “And in those days, butt cheeks were not hanging out.” When she and Sabrina won for Best Collaboration with “Bring Your Love,” she complained about how Sabrina’s handlers waited to return her call, until Sabrina got bleeped for quipping, “My team is shitting themselves backstage.” But she generously spent her speech heaping praise on Sabrina. “She has OCD and so do I,” Madonna said. “We write our lyrics down on pieces of paper, like they did in the 1800s.” Sabrina simply said, “Everybody, Madonna,” before they walked off hand in hand. Trending Stories U2 Dream It All Up Again Madonna’s ‘Danceteria’ Was One of the Great Moments in VMAs History Raye, Sombr, Teddy Swims, Adam Lambert Salute George Michael at MTV VMAs How Trump Became Mob Boss of the United States
THIS DUO!!! @Madonna and @SabrinaAnnLynn take home Best Collaboration at the #VMAs 👯‍♀️🏆 pic.twitter.com/YMlwumHuTd
But the most poignant moment came when Madonna recalled where songs like “Danceteria” came from. “I came to New York to be a dancer,” she said. “Dance is where everything happened for me in my life. I came to life on the dance floor. I found my community on the dance floor. I fell in love with people on the dance floor. And I lost many people I loved on the dance floor.” It was a powerful confession. “Dance brings everybody together, OK?” she said. “We are all equal on the dance floor.” You couldn’t ask for a more succinct summary of everything Madonna’s VMAs performance — or her entire career — has been about.
I’ve been a Madonna fan — and an MTV junkie — since the early days. articles.title_orig: Mexico's Pacific coast braces for Hurricane Polo
articles.title_zh: Mexico's Pacific coast braces for Hurricane Polo
articles.content_orig:
People living on the northern Pacific coast of Mexico are bracing for the arrival of Hurricane Polo, which is forecast to make landfall later on Monday or early on Tuesday.
The category three storm, with maximum sustained winds near 115 mph (185 km/h), is expected to move over the state of Baja California Sur, a region popular with tourists and home to the resort destination of Los Cabos.
Meteorologists at the US-based National Hurricane Center (NHC) have warned of heavy rainfall which could lead to life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
Residents on Sunday stocked up on essentials such as drinking water and food as the storm approached.
The NHC warned of the storm surge Hurricane Polo could unleash, which it said could be accompanied by large and destructive waves.
In Cabo San Lucas, famous for its natural rock arch, the authorities restricted access to the beaches. Some restaurants also closed in the town, which acts as a base for sport fishers and whale watchers.
The regional government of Baja California Sur has ordered schools to remain closed on Monday as a preventive measure.
Governor Víctor Manuel Castro Cosío said temporary shelters had been opened should residents need to be evacuated.
The federal authorities have also deployed thousands of members of the navy and the army along with specialised machinery.
Polo has been slowly moving towards Mexico's coast line.
Meteorologists said it was being fuelled by extremely warm waters caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon.
